newsitem.title: UK: UK's IMRO says few unit trusts in unquoted stock.
newsitem.headline: UK's IMRO says few unit trusts in unquoted stock.

text.p: Britain's Investment Management Regulatory Organisation (IMRO) on Friday published the results of a unit trust industry portfolio review showing that only 13 percent of trusts hold unquoted securities.
The total value of of unquoted or non approved securities avaerages 1.79 percent of the portfolios and only 17 trusts out of 1,669 have reported holdings in pre-listed securities.
IMRO is currently engaged in an investigation of two unit trusts and an investment fund run by Morgan Grenfell Asset Management, a unit of Deutsche Bank.

The three funds were temporarily suspended last week after "possible irregularities" emerged over the valuation of unquoted and pre-listing stocks held by them. Deutsche has since spent over 250 million stg removing the holdings from the funds and pumping in cash to cover redemptions.

"These figures confirm that the vast majority of unit trusts are only invested in quoted securities," said IMRO chief executive Phillip Thorpe. "Even where a few trusts do hold unquoted, non-approved or pre-listed securities, they represent a very small percentage of the portfolio and are well within the requirements of the regulations."
IMRO regulates 171 unit trust managers which account for 100 billion stg, or 10 percent, of funds under management by IMRO-regulated firms.
